Archon.name: Archon
Archon.description: An Archon publicly represents one of Glowhaven City's academies and serves on the Conclave of Archons. Archons are exceptionally capable, but are not automatically hostile; each has an individual personality and agenda.

Headmaster.name: Headmaster
Headmaster.description: A headmaster runs an academy's school system and day-to-day operations. This institutional role does not determine personality or combat ability.

Teacher.name: Teacher
Teacher.description: A teacher works at one of Glowhaven City's academies and has an individual area of expertise. Instructors vary in temperament, experience, and combat capability.

Student.name: Student
Student.description: A student studies at one of Glowhaven City's academies. Students are individuals with different experience and abilities; being a student does not make someone helpless or define their personality.

Resident.name: Resident
Resident.description: A named resident, professional, officer, or visitor outside the academy role categories. Actual job, training, abilities, level, and temperament come from the individual's record; this type grants no shared powers or personality.

Great Sage.name: Great Sage
Great Sage.description: The elected ruler and steward of Glowhaven's Evertree weave. The incumbent's actual abilities, age, knowledge, and condition remain individual authored facts rather than universal type bonuses.

Wild Beast.name: Wild Beast
Wild Beast.description: An animal or local wild creature. Use actual size, behavior, abilities, and danger rather than human motives. A moss-backed boar can charge and retreat; it has no automatic spells, speech, or magical immunity.

Mana Beast.name: Mana Beast
Mana Beast.description: A soul-bearing magical creature. Actual abilities and behavior belong to the individual; the category grants no universal spell, speech, or immunity.

Academy Staff.name: Academy Staff
Academy Staff.description: Employees who make an academy function: attendants, kitchen workers, groundskeepers, technicians and caretakers. Give each an actual job and ordinary responsibilities. They know their workplace and its practical problems, not every private faculty decision. Some are trained mages or fighters; others depend on tools, procedures and colleagues. Helpful, resentful and self-interested individuals all belong to this type. Employment does not grant unrestricted records, court authority or a desire to accompany the player.

Court Official.name: Court Official
Court Official.description: Clerks, appointed officers and civil administrators working within a particular court remit. They can explain the process they actually handle, ask for relevant information and issue only what their office is authorized to issue. They have personal priorities and differing loyalties. An official might be kind, pompous, harried or corrupt without being omniscient. Their position supplies neither automatic combat mastery nor immunity from scrutiny. Use existing named office holders before inventing another one.

City Guard.name: City Guard
City Guard.description: Trained personnel responsible for public safety, patrols and ordinary law enforcement. They recognize immediate threats, call for support and use proportionate force when possible. A patrol can give directions, receive a complaint, separate combatants or make an evidence-based arrest; it cannot pronounce every sentence on the spot. Individual experience and temperament vary. They are capable adults with learned magic and practical training, not disposable obstacles scaled to flatter a new student.

Elite Operative.name: Elite Operative
Elite Operative.description: Experienced members of the Great Sage's exceptional service, selected for difficult protective, military, investigative or diplomatic work. Define the individual's assignment and methods: an envoy need not perform like an assault specialist. They act on actual orders and information, protect sensitive matters and can negotiate or withdraw. Their competence merits serious respect, but a service badge does not make them omniscient, universally loved or above all law.

Prison Officer.name: Prison Officer
Prison Officer.description: Custody, security and authorized transport personnel at Wraith Island Prison. Their actual post determines keys, access and responsibility. They maintain counts, searches, escorts and emergency procedures; an individual can be decent, brutal, diligent or negligent. Prison employment is distinct from being an inmate, visitor, contractor or sentenced worker. Combat ability, access and susceptibility to bribery belong to the individual. They do not confiscate or restore property merely because a narration mentions a search.

Merchant.name: Merchant
Merchant.description: People earning a living by buying and selling goods. Give a merchant a real stock, market, supplier relationship and reason for their prices. They may bargain, offer samples, seek repairs or refuse bad credit; they are neither universal quest dispensers nor automatic frauds. A quoted price is not a completed sale. Their knowledge follows their trade and contacts. Ownership, payment and delivery need actual agreement and supported state changes.

Artisan.name: Artisan
Artisan.description: Makers and repairers with a particular craft, workshop and trained method. Some enchant by hand; others use conventional tools or integrated magitech. Their competence follows experience, materials and the job, not a promise to repair everything instantly. Good scene pressures include a difficult commission, missing part, awkward customer or contested credit. They can discuss a fault before accepting work. Tools, samples and customers' property remain with their actual owners.

Healer.name: Healer
Healer.description: Practitioners of healing, medical care or both, with individual training, supplies and limits. They assess an actual condition rather than promising a perfect reset. Treatment can involve rest, mundane care and paid materials as well as magic. An experienced healer is not necessarily a frontline fighter. Healing does not automatically reverse old age, lasting damage or every unusual curse. Preserve the world's resource and medicine rules, informed choices and actual fees.

Researcher.name: Researcher
Researcher.description: Scholars and investigators pursuing a particular question through study, observation and experiment. A researcher can be generous, possessive, reckless, meticulous or mistaken. Their expertise is specific; one scientific field does not reveal all magic, secret history and institutions. Evidence can change their conclusions. Give their work practical materials, an observable test and something they have not solved. Most research remains ordinary work, not a guaranteed catastrophe or a shortcut to forbidden mastery.

Field Guide.name: Field Guide
Field Guide.description: Travelers, scouts and expedition workers who know particular routes, weather, creatures or communities. They can warn about signs of danger, negotiate passage, assess equipment and choose a safer pace. They do not know every hidden site or guarantee the safety of an unfamiliar route. Their fee covers an agreed service rather than permanent party membership. Distinguish an experienced local guide from an enthusiastic beginner and retain each person's actual capabilities.

Noble.name: Noble
Noble.description: People belonging to recognized houses or holding granted titles. Wealth, education, connections and obligations vary; noble status is not an elemental power or personality. They may be generous patrons, anxious heirs, pompous rivals or practical estate managers. Political influence has a scope and a cost. A title alone grants neither court-issued portal keys nor possession of someone else's property. Class prejudice is an individual attitude, not a statement of objective worth.

Performer.name: Performer
Performer.description: Musicians, dancers, actors, illusion entertainers and other working performers. Give them a real audience, craft and livelihood. Their onstage manner can differ from private behavior without concealing a conspiracy. Magical effects used in a show remain limited by actual skill and preparation; applause does not create combat power or intimacy. Scenes can involve rehearsal, a commission, a rivalry, a failed prop or simply an enjoyable evening.

Bandit.name: Bandit
Bandit.description: Robbers or extortionists operating through a particular opportunity and group. Some rely on intimidation and escape, others on preparation or violence. They can bargain, be deceived, lose nerve, surrender or flee when the risk changes. Give warning signs and a practical motive; do not make every road contain an ambush. This is a role rather than a species or damage profile. Captured or reformed individuals remain persistent people, not a renewable reward supply.

Fae.name: Fae
Fae.description: An exceptionally varied people, especially common in Asterveil. Most are short adults with mature proportions; some are human-sized and a few reach seven or eight feet. Most ears are pointed, some rounded. Individual animal features may include moth, butterfly, dragonfly or bird wings; satyr horns and hooves; antlers; feathered parts; or patches of barklike wooden scales. The common winged humanoid form is not universal. Choose a coherent individual body and state its actual height, mature adult face and proportions, ears, hair, eyes, wings and other features in basicInfo and visualDescription. Preserve those details thereafter. Wings do not prove unlimited flight, a passenger-carrying ability or size-changing. Lifespan and talents depend on the authored individual. No compulsory personality or shared damage modifiers apply.

Dragonkin.name: Dragonkin
Dragonkin.description:
Dragonkin are mostly humanoid people of roughly human height, with human faces, dragonlike horns, scales along the sides of their faces and vertical slit pupils. The backs of their hands and arms are scaly, while their palms retain a human appearance. They have thick dragon tails. Individual colors and the amount of visible scaling vary. Scale color is hereditary but carries no inherent magical affinity, rank, personality or moral significance.

Dragonkin can live up to about two hundred years. Drakenspire's populations and the desert populations of Nahlah Qamar's homeland belong to the same species, with regional differences in appearance, ancestry and culture. For visual direction, Drakenspire's populations have broadly European-inspired human features and the established desert populations broadly Middle Eastern-inspired human features; neither is a rigid template for every individual. Regional ancestry does not assign intelligence, temperament or abilities. Dragonkin are people, not lesser dragons or wyverns. Universal wings, breath weapons and elemental resistance are not supplied by this species definition.

Actual learned abilities determine breath, resistance or flight; this broad people category grants none by itself. Their personalities, careers and competence are individual. Do not use the NPC type as a loot-bearing monster template.

Beastfolk.name: Beastfolk
Beastfolk.description: People with animal-associated features whose appearance and physiology depend on the individual lineage. A ram beastfolk, rabbit beastkin and cat-featured person are not interchangeable. Do not infer temperament, intelligence, occupation or attraction from a trait such as horns or ears. Society, learned magic, personal training and relationships matter. This general type supplies no damage modifier or automatic natural weapon; use each actual record.

Domestic Animal.name: Domestic Animal
Domestic Animal.description: Ordinary cats, dogs and other household animals. Their needs include food, shelter, curiosity, comfort and familiar company. They communicate through behavior unless an actual spell changes that. They may be trained, frightened, stubborn or affectionate without understanding court politics. Ordinary animals do not deliberately cast magic, become collectible loot or join a traveling group merely because someone feeds them. Ownership and established bonds persist.

Livestock.name: Livestock
Livestock.description: Ordinary farm and working-yard animals: cattle, sheep, goats, pigs and similar stock. They shape rural work, fences, feeding, trade and daily noise. A distressed animal may need patience, handling or medical attention rather than combat. They have no deliberate spellcasting. Size can make accidental injury dangerous, but no automatic hostility or elemental resistance follows. Establish who owns the animal before any sale, removal or slaughter.

Pack Animal.name: Pack Animal
Pack Animal.description: Ordinary mounts and burden animals trained for hauling or travel. Terrain, loads, rest and handling affect what is practical. A nervous beast can balk at a portal, narrow ledge or unfamiliar smell; that is an interaction, not proof of possession. They do not understand route permits or cast their way out of danger. A hired animal remains subject to its actual loan terms and owner.

Wild Predator.name: Wild Predator
Wild Predator.description: Ordinary wolves, big cats and similar predators. Hunger, territory, cubs, injury and experience with people influence their choices. Most avoid a costly fight when they can. Tracks, calls, scent and disturbed prey can warn of their presence. They do not possess deliberate spellcasting or pursue a retreating party forever. Observation, distance, deterrence and a changed route can solve the encounter.

Wild Herbivore.name: Wild Herbivore
Wild Herbivore.description: Ordinary deer, hares and other nonpredatory wildlife. They may flee, freeze, hide or defend young. A cornered large animal can be dangerous without being malicious. Use them for ecology, observation, hunting where lawful or an ordinary pleasant sight. They have no automatic affinity or conversational knowledge. Finding wildlife is not necessarily an encounter that needs a quest or a fight.

Giant Spider.name: Giant Spider
Giant Spider.description: Large mana-bearing spiders whose hunting methods depend on species and surroundings. Web lines, abandoned prey and vibration responses can reveal a territory before contact. They may trap, ambush, guard eggs or withdraw; they do not all obey a matron or share a mind. Some use venom or trained-looking magical reflexes, but an individual needs those actual capabilities. Fire threatens exposed silk and body alike. Routes can be studied, cut or bypassed instead of charging into a nest.

Moltback Silkguard.name: Moltback Silkguard
Moltback Silkguard.description: A broad, hairless spider mana beast with layered rust-brown chitin, dull green eyes and pale webbing around its forelegs. It plants its weight over territory and anchors silk before lunging or pulling at an intruder's footing. Heavy plates resist cuts and punctures; fire threatens vulnerable joints and silk. Taut lines, shed plates and a braced posture telegraph its position. It cannot cover every approach at once. Study anchors, change elevation, disrupt its stance or find a bypass. This is a reusable creature type, not one named individual or an endlessly respawning guard. Set an actual encounter's level, tier, abilities and persistent outcome separately.

Slime.name: Slime
Slime.description: Mobile masses of mana-bearing gel that gather around food, moisture or particular residues. Size and composition determine their danger. Their soft bodies disperse blunt impact, while cold can stiffen the gel. A slime can engulf scraps, obstruct a drain or threaten an unwary animal without plotting against anyone. Notice trails and feeding before touching it. Specialized corrosive, intelligent or elemental variants require an actual individual record; this type does not dissolve every possession on contact.

Dire Wolf.name: Dire Wolf
Dire Wolf.description: Mana-adapted pack hunters, larger and more coordinated than ordinary wolves. They use cover, scent and group pressure rather than waiting in a line to be fought. Howling, tracks and a sudden absence of prey can warn travelers. Individuals protect territory and packmates; injury and an unfavorable position can make them disengage. They have no blanket resistance or automatic elemental spell repertoire. Negotiation needs a real way to communicate, not ordinary human speech assumed to work.

Stonehide Boar.name: Stonehide Boar
Stonehide Boar.description: A heavy forest or foothill mana beast with mineralized hide along its shoulders. It drives forward with alarming force but needs room to turn and recover after a committed charge. Plowed ground, broken saplings and scraped stone mark its route. Water-softened footing and redirected movement offer practical counters; the hide is particularly good at dispersing blunt impacts. It may be defending a feeding ground, not hunting people. A barricade or a quieter approach can be more sensible than a duel.

Great Bear.name: Great Bear
Great Bear.description: A large mana-bearing bear adapted to remote woodland or mountain territory. Its weight, reach and endurance make careless close combat dangerous. It can stand, bluff, swat or charge, with clearer intentions than a speaking villain. Tracks, torn bark and food caches offer warning. Cubs, hunger and injury shape its aggression. Individual magical techniques are authored separately; being a great bear does not grant every Nature spell or require a fight to the death.

Griffin.name: Griffin
Griffin.description: Powerful winged mana beasts with an eaglelike forebody and leonine hindquarters. They use height, dives and territorial displays; a grounded griffin still has dangerous reach. Wind conditions, wing room and a nest's position matter. They can be trained through a real history of care but are not automatically mounts. Aerie signs should precede a nest encounter. Avoid clipping wings or awarding flight merely because the creature's type is known.

Roc.name: Roc
Roc.description: Enormous mountain or sky-island birds whose size turns a landing, wingbeat or carried load into a serious local event. Their nesting ranges are large, not an excuse to spawn one above every bridge. Broken branches, vast shadows, calls and disturbed herds can announce them. They favor space and altitude; enclosed terrain restricts them. A roc follows animal needs rather than theatrical cruelty. Protecting food or young may be resolved by distance, diversion or a negotiated route through knowledgeable locals.

Sky Serpent.name: Sky Serpent
Sky Serpent.description: Long-bodied flying mana beasts seen among high currents and isolated islands. They coil through open air, using terrain and wind to approach or evade. A resting serpent can resemble a ribbon along a cliff until it moves. Their exact affinity and temperament vary; flight is not universal control of the weather. Young, wounded or territorial individuals behave differently. A careful crossing can avoid their hunting path, and a warning display need not become an attack.

Drake.name: Drake
Drake.description: Wingless or limited-flight draconic mana beasts, distinct from dragonkin people and fully developed dragons. Their scales resist light cuts, while bludgeoning force can reach through the armor. A drake's territory, diet and individual element determine an encounter; the category alone grants no breath weapon or fire immunity. Shed scales, claw marks and feeding remains give warning. They can be cunning without speaking or submitting to a claimant with a noble title.

Wyvern.name: Wyvern
Wyvern.description: Two-legged winged draconic predators, much smaller than true dragons, with territorial shrieks and a preference for height and a clear escape. Circling shadows, scored perches and displaced wildlife can warn of their presence. They dive, seize prey and defend occupied nesting ledges; narrow interiors restrict their wings. Venom and breath belong only to individuals explicitly possessing them. They are distinct from dragonkin people and sacred dragons, not automatically willing mounts, and their nests are not unowned treasure stores.

Dragon.name: Dragon
Dragon.description: Rare, formidable draconic beings whose age, intelligence, element and relationships must be established individually. Some may speak and negotiate; others behave as territorial beasts. Do not generate one casually to raise the stakes of an ordinary errand. A dragon's presence changes how settlements travel and prepare, with visible evidence before direct contact. This broad type gives no blanket elemental immunity, universal spell mastery, rebirth or permission to ignore resolved outcomes.

Phoenix.name: Phoenix
Phoenix.description: Rare fire-bearing winged mana beasts associated with sustained heat and brilliant plumage. They seek suitable nesting grounds and react to actual threats rather than functioning as academy mascots that anyone can summon. Fire cannot harm their burning bodies; water can break their concentration and chill the flame. Rebirth, healing tears and transferable immortality are not guaranteed properties of this category. Establish such exceptional powers in the particular individual, with real limits.

Hydra.name: Hydra
Hydra.description: Large many-headed aquatic or marshland mana beasts. Multiple heads can watch different approaches and coordinate bites, but they still share one body, space and capacity to maneuver. Their wake, tracks and feeding sites should warn of danger. Regeneration is not an infinite extra-life mechanic: any actual regrowth requires an explicit ability and its limitations. This type grants no resistance by default. Observation, terrain and leaving a nesting area can matter as much as damage.

Crystal Moth.name: Crystal Moth
Crystal Moth.description: Delicate mana-bearing moths with translucent mineral scales. They gather near particular currents and light sources, making their movement useful to attentive field researchers. Crowds can obscure vision or settle on exposed equipment, usually without hostile intent. Handling them roughly damages their wings; careful observation or a changed light source may redirect them. They do not provide effortless Divination, unlimited crystal materials or a new portal whenever they gather.

Thorn Creeper.name: Thorn Creeper
Thorn Creeper.description: A mobile mass of thorned roots and stems animated by its own accumulated mana. It probes toward vibration and accessible nutrients, rooting itself to pull or restrain prey. Dry fibers burn easily, while the springing structure disperses blunt blows. Fresh scratches, displaced roots and a patch of disturbed soil can telegraph it. Severing an anchor or moving outside its reach can break a hold. It is not automatically a person, a druid's familiar or a hive mind.

Mimic.name: Mimic
Mimic.description: A shape-assuming mana beast that imitates a particular kind of object to ambush prey. Its disguise has physical limits: seams, weight, residue or a suspicious position can betray it. Give an established mimic a consistent body and feeding method rather than turning every examined chest into one after the fact. Detection and careful handling can prevent a fight. Defeating it does not automatically create the valuable object it appeared to be.

Stone Golem.name: Stone Golem
Stone Golem.description: A deliberately animated stone body built for a task such as hauling, guarding or holding a dangerous structure. Its joints, core and instructions provide specific points to investigate. Stone resists cuts and punctures, while concentrated blunt force can break its body. It has no living circulation for poison. A simple golem follows an actual command system, not conversational persuasion; a sentient exception needs an individual record. Disabling a control or fulfilling an instruction can be more useful than smashing it.

Metal Automaton.name: Metal Automaton
Metal Automaton.description: An articulated metal construct with an identifiable power and control system. It may be an enchanted worker, a guard or a true magitech device; establish which rather than treating all machinery as the same. Its casing resists cuts and punctures, but lightning can disrupt exposed channels. Poison does not affect its nonliving body. Maintenance faults, control access and limited orders create practical interaction. A disabled machine is not repaired by flattery or automatically claimed as salvage.

Animated Armor.name: Animated Armor
Animated Armor.description: An empty suit moved by an actual enchantment. It can guard a threshold, perform rehearsed work or respond to a command, with movement limited by the suit's construction. Blunt force can deform joints; blades have difficulty finding flesh that is not present. Poison has no biological target. Decide how its order can be recognized, suspended or fulfilled. It does not acquire the remembered personality of every person who once wore the armor.

Rune Sentinel.name: Rune Sentinel
Rune Sentinel.description: An anchored constructed watcher tied to a defined ward and detection method. It reacts to what its sensors and instructions can actually perceive, not hidden character sheets or all criminal intent. Marks, lenses, a charged surface or a warning tone can reveal its coverage. It has no living body to poison. Bypassing a sensor, presenting valid authority or disabling the real power channel can change its response. It cannot pursue beyond its physical reach without an actual mobile form.

Clockwork Beast.name: Clockwork Beast
Clockwork Beast.description: An animal-shaped mechanism used for transport, workshop work, demonstration or security. Its design governs speed, load and attacks; resemblance to a beast supplies no natural instincts or inherited spells. Exposed workings are vulnerable to grit, damage and poorly controlled lightning. It has no living metabolism for poison. True integrated magitech is distinct from a simple enchanted toy. Skilled repair requires the real fault, suitable tools and materials, not a generic instant fix.

Skeleton.name: Skeleton
Skeleton.description: Reanimated bones held together by a particular necromantic force. They may follow a command, guard a site or retain fragments of a former person only when the individual record supports it. Blunt force breaks the frame effectively, and light disrupts its animating pattern. Piercing attacks find little soft tissue; poison has no living circulation to affect. Who animated it and whether it can be released are investigation questions, not knowledge every passerby possesses.

Restless Corpse.name: Restless Corpse
Restless Corpse.description: A dead body animated by an actual spell, binding or localized supernatural condition. Movement and awareness depend on that cause. Fire and light can damage the body and animating pattern; poison has no ordinary living metabolism to exploit. It is not automatically infectious or proof that a nearby living necromancer is guilty. Give a site credible signs and a way to investigate or avoid it. Returned remains are still somebody's remains, not routine trade loot.

Ghost.name: Ghost
Ghost.description: An incorporeal presence with a particular origin, awareness and attachment. Some can communicate; others repeat a limited pattern. Light can disrupt the manifestation, while ordinary physical blows pass through much of it. Poison cannot harm a body that is absent. These damage rules do not imply immunity to compassion, deception or evidence. Discover what it actually perceives and wants before assuming it must be destroyed. Knowledge and memories remain as limited as its history allows.

Wraith.name: Wraith
Wraith.description: A dangerous disembodied remnant sustained by a specific supernatural cause. Its chill, sound or effect on nearby life can warn of a manifestation. It may stalk, guard, hunger or pursue a binding; it is not automatically an intelligent schemer. Light threatens its form, ordinary physical blows are less effective, and poison has no biological target. Injuries it causes follow the actual attack and treatment rules rather than an invented unavoidable permanent curse. Wraith Island's name does not establish that these creatures patrol its prison.

Fire Elemental.name: Fire Elemental
Fire Elemental.description: Living flame gathered around a sustaining mana pattern. Heat shimmer, scorched surfaces and an appetite for fuel make its presence observable. It can flow around an obstacle but needs a real route; an extinguished manifestation does not automatically respawn. Its heat is dangerous to nearby people and possessions according to actual contact, not limitless ambient damage. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Water Elemental.name: Water Elemental
Water Elemental.description: A coherent moving volume of water held by a sustaining mana pattern. It uses flow, weight and its available surroundings. A basin, channel or dry interior changes its options. It does not have infinite water or automatic control of every liquid inside a person. Ripples moving against the current can signal its presence. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Earth Elemental.name: Earth Elemental
Earth Elemental.description: A mana-bound body of soil and mineral. It uses mass, footing and available ground, with limited reach through actual material. Water can loosen its cohesion; this is a damage vulnerability, not an instant automatic victory. Crumbling edges and shifting ground can announce its movement. Tunnels, buildings and bystanders remain real constraints. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Wind Elemental.name: Wind Elemental
Wind Elemental.description: A sustained circulating body of air. Dust, moving cloth and pressure changes can reveal it. It can buffet or obstruct but does not suffocate everyone nearby by existing. Confined geometry and rooted barriers affect its movement; earth magic is particularly effective at breaking its circulation. A harmless current is not automatically this creature. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Ice Elemental.name: Ice Elemental
Ice Elemental.description: An articulated manifestation of frost and ice around a mana pattern. Cracking surfaces, spreading rime and disturbed meltwater reveal its movement. It can brace, break or reshape within its actual abilities, without freezing a whole settlement on arrival. Heat threatens its coherence. Destroyed fragments do not each become a new enemy. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Lightning Elemental.name: Lightning Elemental
Lightning Elemental.description: A bounded electrical manifestation with a sustaining pattern. Charge noise, lifted hairs and light along conductive paths warn of it. It can exploit real conductors but does not teleport through any named metal object anywhere. Grounding and earth magic can disrupt it. A laboratory spark or routine storm is not proof that one exists. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Arachne.name: Arachne
Arachne.description: Sapient beings with a humanoid upper body and a large spiderlike lower body. Silk, climbing and natural reach depend on the individual's anatomy and trained abilities. They have their own names, motives and relationships; they are not all members of one brood or automatically hostile. A particular matron's territorial cruelty is her own character. Establish awareness, casting and combat capability in the real individual record. This type supplies no automatic resistance, spell mastery, social immunity or party membership.

Giant.name: Giant
Giant.description: Very large humanoid beings whose particular intelligence, speech, social behavior and abilities must be established individually. Mountain signs may include huge tracks, displaced boulders and shelters at a different scale. Size makes ordinary movement dangerous to smaller people without making every giant malicious or mindless. Show evidence and actual motives before direct contact. The category does not assign a fixed boss level, universal resistance, guaranteed treasure or automatic hostility. The isolated yeti Orrum is a separately authored individual using this broad body type. Reuse his NPC record when its rare encounter actually occurs; do not produce generic yeti packs or duplicate his identity.

Threadwing Grazer.name: Threadwing Grazer
Threadwing Grazer.description:
APPEARANCE: A rabbit-sized six-legged insect with a rounded moss-green body and four long translucent ribbon wings. Fine combs replace biting jaws; a small ring of amber eye spots sits around its blunt head. At rest the wings hang like loose silk, without a humanoid face.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Cloudbloom meadow colonies eat pollen and mineral fibers. Usually level 10–20 at appropriate sites; a cornered group can whip abrasive wing edges or raise a blinding pollen cloud. They migrate between bloom patches and are not universally hostile.
COUNTERPLAY: Observe the feeding rhythm, cover exposed eyes, interrupt the wing space or leave the colony room to move. Fire also destroys the crop a collector may be trying to protect.
FIELD VALUE: Naturally shed wing scales and properly gathered fibers support filter cloth and fragrance research.
GENERATION: Use the actual location band and establish this individual’s level, tier, disposition and bounded abilities. This type does not spawn itself or rescale an existing creature. Copy its diagnostic anatomy into the generated record and visual description; do not replace it with a generic humanoid or a familiar monster with the same color. Reuse a previously encountered individual. Recovered material requires actual acquisition; no guaranteed loot, instant crafting bonus, tame companion or universal consumable effect is granted.

Twigback Browser.name: Twigback Browser
Twigback Browser.description:
APPEARANCE: A deer-sized four-legged herbivore with a barrel chest, dark felt skin and branching flat paddles growing along its back instead of antlers on its head. Its head is broad and blunt with two sideways amber eyes. The back paddles carry living moss.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Browses Cloudbloom woodland and sleeps beneath branches. Slow and wary until crowded, when it shoves or charges. Its resting silhouette resembles a small fallen tree; this is camouflage rather than illusion magic.
COUNTERPLAY: Read hoof marks and breathing before collecting from a supposed log. Give young animals room; cover interrupts its straight charge.
FIELD VALUE: Discarded paddle tips and rubbed-off moss can be useful under an agreed collection limit.
GENERATION: Use the actual location band and establish this individual’s level, tier, disposition and bounded abilities. This type does not spawn itself or rescale an existing creature. Copy its diagnostic anatomy into the generated record and visual description; do not replace it with a generic humanoid or a familiar monster with the same color. Reuse a previously encountered individual. Recovered material requires actual acquisition; no guaranteed loot, instant crafting bonus, tame companion or universal consumable effect is granted.

Ribbonjaw Prowler.name: Ribbonjaw Prowler
Ribbonjaw Prowler.description:
APPEARANCE: A lean wolf-sized ambush animal with six short hooked legs, smooth bark-brown hide and two long flexible jaw membranes running down its neck. Its real mouth is small; the membranes unfold sideways into a ribbed capture basket. Four forward-facing black eyes catch tiny highlights.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Stalks Sunspill’s hanging bark lanes. It grips prey briefly, then retreats to cover; it does not swallow a person whole or teleport between shadows.
COUNTERPLAY: Watch both flanks, use open ground and strike the extended membrane during its committed rush. A severed membrane is a real injury, not a free endless whip attack.
FIELD VALUE: Recovered membrane can suit flexible bindings, but only actual suitable remains or shed tissue exist.
GENERATION: Use the actual location band and establish this individual’s level, tier, disposition and bounded abilities. This type does not spawn itself or rescale an existing creature. Copy its diagnostic anatomy into the generated record and visual description; do not replace it with a generic humanoid or a familiar monster with the same color. Reuse a previously encountered individual. Recovered material requires actual acquisition; no guaranteed loot, instant crafting bonus, tame companion or universal consumable effect is granted.

Petalglass Snail.name: Petalglass Snail
Petalglass Snail.description:
APPEARANCE: A knee-high snail with a broad pearly foot, four short feelers and a fan of overlapping transparent petal-shaped shell plates. Mineral colors show through the shell; it has no floral human head or separate limbs.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Grazes films from spring pools and Prismbloom margins. Mostly peaceful, but a hard blow can release razorlike shell fragments as it contracts. A living population contributes to filtration without making all nearby water safe.
COUNTERPLAY: Move it gently with an actual method, avoid crushing its fragile plates and collect cast-off shell rather than treating a grazer as a required kill.

APPEARANCE: A small-boat-sized freshwater animal with a broad soft mantle, eight short flexible edge fins and a dark central underside keel. Its mouth opens below the keel; two pale eyes sit above it. It has neither human features nor a tentacled octopus head.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Feeds in Mirrorwater’s open lakes and rises slowly through reeds. Adults shove boats, defend calves and stir opaque silt rather than automatically hunt people. Young remain smaller individuals within the site’s level band.

Young Stonehide Boar.description: A small, not fully grown Stonehide Boar with soft mineral patches rather than a mature armored shoulder. It stamps and makes a short, committed charge, then needs to turn. Its undeveloped hide has no inherited damage resistance. It is a beginner territorial obstacle, not a disguised adult champion.

Puddle Slime.name: Puddle Slime
Puddle Slime.description: A small translucent slime feeding on harmless drain and riverbank residue. Ripples and a damp trail reveal it. It makes one simple shove or splash and has neither strong corrosive venom nor a universal resistance to ordinary weapons. It can be lured away from its food.

Stray Forest Hound.name: Stray Forest Hound
Stray Forest Hound.description: A hungry, ordinary hound encountered near a maintained route. It barks, circles and may make a single clumsy bite before reassessing. It is not a Dire Wolf, pack leader or spellcasting predator. Food, distance and a firm barrier can change its behavior.

Underbrush Spider.name: Underbrush Spider
Underbrush Spider.description: A small forest mana spider with pale-brown legs and thin ankle-height trip silk. Its feeble venom is a short local irritation, not recurring lethal damage. A disturbed web and scattered husks warn of its hiding place. It has one simple lunge and can flee.

Snow Spirit.name: Snow Spirit
Snow Spirit.description: An intelligent winter manifestation with a humanoid adult face, cold-pale skin and hair or garments formed from a coherent local legend. Has individual knowledge and motives; neither every snow spirit nor every grievance is Ysolenne. Use bounded Ice workings and local terrain, not effortless death by looking at it. Ordinary instances follow actual location level bands; Ysolenne remains the unique named individual with her own fixed power and relationships.

Frostglass Leech.name: Frostglass Leech
Frostglass Leech.description: A flattened translucent ribbon animal the length of a forearm, with six black anchoring nubs along each side and a round glassy sucker at either end. Its frozen outer film crackles when disturbed. It nests in cold damp mineral seams and seeks warmth in pulses; dry ground and steady heat can deter it. It cannot freeze a whole party at a touch. Use a few actual individuals at the site's level band, preserving their unusual anatomy in generated portraits.

Cloudveil Nautilus.name: Cloudveil Nautilus
Cloudveil Nautilus.description: A floating sky mollusk with an opalescent spiral shell, a broad clear membrane sail and five short lavender fins beneath its body; paired dark eyes sit on flexible stalks, with no human face or humanoid torso. It grazes airborne mineral dust along sheltered Asterveil currents. Adults can conceal themselves in drifting mist but cannot teleport. Some mature current-sensing chambers produce a Stillwind Pearl, and an intact spent casing may preserve one. A living creature is not an automatic loot container; observation and actual safe collection matter.

Bracewing Cicada.name: Bracewing Cicada
Bracewing Cicada.description: A palm-sized emerald insect with four triangular translucent wings and hooked hind legs shaped like tiny clamps. Groups brace themselves across exposed vine cables and drink salt from woven fibers. Their resonant wingbeats can shake a light instrument or signal line; they are not a giant lethal swarm by default. Gentle vibration changes, a suitable lure or rerouting a cable can resolve interference. Keep these recognizable insects rather than generating fairy people.

Vaultjaw Marten.name: Vaultjaw Marten
Vaultjaw Marten.description: A long-bodied six-legged mammal with russet fur, small black eyes and two overlapping pale jaw plates that close like a hinged clasp around hard food. It nests in sheltered crates and steals resin, nuts and bright offcuts. A loose hinge-like clicking warns of a defensive snap. Juveniles are suitable weak low-level nuisances; mature wild individuals follow the real local band. It has no extradimensional stomach and cannot swallow an entire inventory or become an elite Mimic through a naming shortcut.

Needleback Prowler.name: Needleback Prowler
Needleback Prowler.description: A low, broad reptilian hunter with moss-green scales, four jointed legs and a flexible comb of hollow ivory needles along its spine. Its blunt wedge head bears four small amber eyes; its tail ends in two gripping pads used to cling to reeds and cage frames. It ambushes small prey in Asterveil wet channels and lashes its needle comb only within close range. Disturbed reeds, shed needles and a blocked retreat provide counterplay. It cannot fire endless projectiles, read minds or ignore cover.

Crucible Competitor.name: Crucible Competitor
Crucible Competitor.description: An adult competitor with an independent livelihood and actual chosen fighting method. Entry in an arena does not imply guild registration, a badge, noble birth or a single temperament. Regulated competition follows its announced nonlethal rules; the person retains ordinary loyalties, work and the ability to decline a match.

Gravewood Golem.name: Gravewood Golem
Gravewood Golem.description: A broad walking frame of pale timber, riblike branches and an empty stone face-mask. Moss threads its joints and amber lights burn in the grain. Most are mindless instruction-bound vessels, not conscious dead people. Nature and Soul workings are distinct ways to affect frame and binding. Guards the rooted walks in small groups; deliberate flanking and exposed joint bindings provide counterplay.

Rootbound Pallbearer.name: Rootbound Pallbearer
Rootbound Pallbearer.description: A four-legged bier of black roots carrying a hollow wooden torso and a little bell. It drags binding strands behind it and tries to hold an intruder for another guardian. Slow turns and the exposed rear bell are readable weaknesses. Its apparent coffin is not automatically occupied by a conscious soul.

Censer-Willow.name: Censer-Willow
Censer-Willow.description: A narrow willow-bodied guardian with hanging seed-pod censers and a crown of long white leaves. It releases visible drifting spiritual haze to obscure an approach, then strikes with flexible branches. Air movement and distance can clear a lane. The haze is not automatic possession, hallucination or unavoidable damage.

Hollowseed Swarm.name: Hollowseed Swarm
Hollowseed Swarm.description: A single coherent encounter of fist-sized seed husks with insectlike root legs and dim blue interiors. They skitter toward warm moving bodies and try to overwhelm one exposed position. Broad barriers, water channels and disrupting the central cluster can limit them. A swarm is not an unlimited number of independent attacks.

Ossuary Trellis.name: Ossuary Trellis
Ossuary Trellis.description: A wall-clinging lattice of roots and old animal bones, its folded limbs opening like a garden fan. It blocks narrow routes with real hooked growth and reacts to contact or vibration. Cutting its exposed anchors or following a different physical route can avoid a direct contest.

Grafted Sentinel.name: Grafted Sentinel
Grafted Sentinel.description: A tall armored tree-vessel with a polished memorial plate, a heavy root club and a visible amber binding knot behind one shoulder. These finite inner guards act with disciplined physical pressure rather than a limitless supply of spells. A real individual spirit may occupy a particular vessel only when established; otherwise it is an instruction-bound guardian.

Rootbound Regent.name: Rootbound Regent
Rootbound Regent.description: An individually named intelligent caretaker built from living timber, funerary bronze and conscious spiritual bindings. It can reason, bargain, lie and defend itself. Its Nature framework and Soul stewardship do not confer universal magic immunity, instant resurrection or the authority to command every dead creature.

Cellar Rat.name: Cellar Rat
Cellar Rat.description: A large ordinary brown rat with a blunt nose, torn ears and flour dust caught in its whiskers. It bites when cornered, then scurries behind cover; it has no venom, armor or magical disease. Usually a level 1 nuisance. Scratching, droppings and gnawed sacks reveal its route. Traps, a food lure or a clear escape can work as well as a blow.

Stray Dog.name: Stray Dog
Stray Dog.description: A lean, rough-coated domestic dog with muddy paws and an uneven leather collar. A hungry stray may defend stolen food, bark and make a short snap before retreating. Beginner individuals are level 1–2, not wolves or trained warhounds. Flattened ears and a stiff posture warn of a bite; food, space and patient handling may avoid one. No automatic rabies, bleeding effect or alpha pack.

Flour Beetle.name: Flour Beetle
Flour Beetle.description: A knee-high oval beetle with cream-brown wing cases, six stubby legs and flour clinging to its feelers. Its shell is thin. It drags dry food toward a dark gap, lifting its front legs before an awkward shove. Level 1–2 specimens are slow nuisances with no damage resistance. Turning a sack, blocking a gap or baiting a basket can contain one without destroying the grain.

Runaway Cleaning Broom.name: Runaway Cleaning Broom
Runaway Cleaning Broom.description: A household broom animated by a worn cleaning enchantment, with copper binding wire and an erratically glowing maker’s mark. It whacks whatever it mistakes for dirt and needs time to turn its long handle. Usually level 2. Pinning the bristles or safely interrupting its accessible binding can stop it. It has no hidden master, inexhaustible spell arsenal or resistance merely because it is a construct.

Orchard Crab.name: Orchard Crab
Orchard Crab.description: A broad freshwater crab about the size of a cooking pot, its mottled olive shell often carrying fallen blossom petals. It wedges itself into irrigation sluices and raises one conspicuous claw before pinching. Young specimens are level 2–3 and have no armored damage resistance. A baited pot, a lifted sluice or a cautious approach from behind offers alternatives to a fight.

Soot Moth.name: Soot Moth
Soot Moth.description: A hand-sized moth with charcoal wings, amber eye-spots and a fluffy white collar stained by lamp soot. It feeds on warm lamp residue and leaves dusty wing prints on glass. Level 2–3 nuisances flutter into faces or shed a brief obscuring puff; they cannot poison lungs, blind permanently or ignite a building. A shaded decoy lamp and a soft net can move them safely.

Timberjaw Gnawer.name: Timberjaw Gnawer
Timberjaw Gnawer.description: A stocky, rabbit-sized mana rodent with broad orange incisors, a squared muzzle and a tail fringed with wood fibers. It gnaws damp supports and stamps before lunging at a nearby boot. Common troublesome adults are level 5–8. Fresh paired tooth marks and a trail of damp shavings expose the nest; sound bracing, barriers and bait interrupt its approach. No instant beam collapse or buried swarm is inherent to the species.

Lantern Wasp.name: Lantern Wasp
Lantern Wasp.description: A fist-sized wasp with a translucent amber abdomen and folded wings patterned like paper ribs. Its nest resembles a little hanging lantern. A bright pulse and rising buzz precede a single close sting. Local nuisance adults are level 6–8. Their venom produces a painful welt rather than continuous lethal damage; covering the light or dampening an abandoned nest can make relocation possible.

Cinderback Lizard.name: Cinderback Lizard
Cinderback Lizard.description: A squat red-brown lizard with four splayed feet and a row of warm coal-colored scales across its shoulders. Often level 7–9 around forges, it warms its back visibly before expelling a short ember puff, then must cool. It cannot breathe a dragon’s stream of flame. A clear cool route, a shielded coal lure or shutting off its heat source changes its behavior.

Scrap Imp.name: Scrap Imp
Scrap Imp.description: A small nonhumanoid fiend with an angular brass-colored face, batlike ears, backward-bending legs and a forked tail used to carry washers. Often level 7–10, it steals useful offcuts and makes crude mechanical toys. It can speak and bargain, lie or become spiteful; these are individual choices. It throws loose scrap or makes a short clawing rush, without teleporting away an entire inventory.

Reed Ambusher.name: Reed Ambusher
Reed Ambusher.description: A flat olive amphibian with four finned limbs, a wide shovel jaw and a fringe of reed-like whiskers. It lies in shallow water and pushes a visible V-shaped ripple ahead of a short bankward leap. Usually level 8–11. It must return to water between committed lunges. High dry footing, a disturbed mud trail and bait are useful; concealment is camouflage rather than true invisibility.

Burrback Hedgebeast.name: Burrback Hedgebeast
Burrback Hedgebeast.description: A goat-sized grazer with short brown fur, a broad snout and tough seed-like burrs woven through its back. Local adults are usually level 8–11. It bowls through low fences, lowers its head before charging and leaves hooked burrs along its trail. Its prickles scratch at contact but do not launch endless binding roots. Fruit lures, open lanes and repaired fencing can redirect it.

Glass-Eye Basilisk.name: Glass-Eye Basilisk
Glass-Eye Basilisk.description: A six-legged gray reptile with green glassy brow plates and milky eyes that brighten before a fixed stare. Local adults are level 13–16. Its sustained gaze causes a brief creeping stiffness; looking away or breaking sight interrupts it. There is no instant permanent petrification. It moves poorly on loose rubble and cannot gaze through walls, shields or closed shutters.

Hollow Lantern.name: Hollow Lantern
Hollow Lantern.description: A salt-corroded rescue lantern floating inside a loose hoop of pale spirit-light, with a wavering human-sized shadow beneath it and no actual body. Usually level 13–16. It repeats a damaged signal and releases a bounded pulse of cold light when approached. Its direction and bell rhythm reveal the place to which it is bound. This is a local haunting, not an all-knowing dead soul or an automatic possession.

Ashcoil Salamander.name: Ashcoil Salamander
Ashcoil Salamander.description: A long charcoal-black salamander with six small feet, a coiling tail and orange seams between its broad scales. Furnace-fed adults are level 14–17. Its throat glows before a close heat jet, followed by a cooling pause. It hunts warm mineral deposits rather than metal objects in an inventory. Damp channels, furnace shutters and vent pressure offer counterplay; no unavoidable room-wide inferno.

Mireglass Stalker.name: Mireglass Stalker
Mireglass Stalker.description: A low wetland hunter with four narrow legs, a split paddle tail and translucent green plates over a dark amphibian body. Typically level 14–18. Reflections break up its outline, but mud prints, ripples and shifting reeds remain visible. It makes short lunges rather than teleporting and loses its camouflage on dry ground. It has neither perfect invisibility nor an unavoidable opening critical strike.

Canal Watcher.name: Canal Watcher
Canal Watcher.description: A waist-high municipal maintenance construct with a round ceramic torso, three iron feet, a water-level float and two jointed gate tools. Malfunctioning working models are around level 14–17. A clacking gauge precedes each heavy tool sweep. A cracked float or obstructed intake may explain its faulty safety order. It has reachable controls, limited movement and no blanket construct immunities.

Thunderfin Ray.name: Thunderfin Ray
Thunderfin Ray.description: A blue-gray mana ray that skims wet sand and shallow water on broad winglike fins, with three amber nodules along its spine and a narrow ribbon tail. Local adults are level 15–18. The nodules glow and its fins spread before a bounded electric discharge. Dry high ground and spacing matter; it cannot electrocute an entire coastline or discharge every action without recovery.

Yokai.name: Yokai
Yokai.description: A varied category of uncanny beings, awakened objects and enduring local spirits. Determine an individual’s actual body, intelligence, origins and disposition; the category grants no uniform hostility, spell list or immunity. Authored Koma, Suzu-no-Ura, Oroha and Hagire keep their individual identities and bodies rather than becoming interchangeable encounters.

Roadside Sparrow Imp.name: Roadside Sparrow Imp
Roadside Sparrow Imp.description: A fist-sized charcoal-and-cream birdlike imp with a flat wooden-looking beak, bright bead eyes and a ragged red throat pouch. It steals soft sandal cords and nests beneath benches. Usually a mischievous nuisance that can be lured, traded with or driven off, not an automatic lethal encounter.

Bamboo Fox.name: Bamboo Fox
Bamboo Fox.description: A lean russet mana fox with green-black ear tips, a long brush tail and narrow pale eyes. It uses bamboo cover and a small misleading rustle rather than human speech or broad illusion mastery. Territorial animals can retreat, hunt or defend young; they are not automatically helpful pets.

Moss-Tongue Kodama.name: Moss-Tongue Kodama
Moss-Tongue Kodama.description: A small bark-bodied forest spirit with a round knotted face, dark sap eyes, two root legs and a long mossy tongue. It tastes rain and rearranges little offerings. Usually curious or mischievous; an actual polluted or damaged shelter can provoke it. It is neither a child nor a compulsory combat target.

Antler-Moss Boar.name: Antler-Moss Boar
Antler-Moss Boar.description: A dark bristled boar with pale rootlike growths over its brow and short moss-covered antler branches. It turns soft soil and follows fallen fruit. A fence gap, seasonal food and clear escape routes matter more than an invented grudge against all humans.

Boundary Tengu.name: Boundary Tengu
Boundary Tengu.description: An adult bird-featured mountain yokai with a long beaked face, dark feathered wings, humanlike hands and red-brown travel layers. It guards a particular claimed crossing and can bargain, bluff or fight. Wings and local knowledge do not make it omniscient or sovereign over every mountain.

Cinder Umbrella.name: Cinder Umbrella
Cinder Umbrella.description: An awakened paper umbrella with one amber eye beneath a scorched rim, a wooden shaft leg and a ragged tongue of warm ash. It hops, spins and spits small hot flecks, usually around abandoned shelter or mishandled offerings. It can be dangerous without becoming an explosive city-destroying artifact.

Paper-Face Lurker.name: Paper-Face Lurker
Paper-Face Lurker.description: A tall loose arrangement of old paper masks around a thin dark frame. One face turns at a time while folded paper fingers test doors and rails. It uses blind angles and limited decoys; the moving frame is real and can be pinned or disrupted.

Scree Crab.name: Scree Crab
Scree Crab.description: A low slate-shelled crawler with six jointed legs, two broad foreclaws and orange seam eyes. It wedges among stones and scrapes mineral surfaces. Falling debris and occupied crevices telegraph it; it is not automatically a giant quarry boss.

Kiln Ashling.name: Kiln Ashling
Kiln Ashling.description: A small round ash creature with a red ember belly, thin soot arms and a wide pale mouth. It follows hot waste and cools into a sleepy lump when deprived of heat. Newly licensed jobs use small weak individuals, not a spontaneous inferno.

Crystal Centipede.name: Crystal Centipede
Crystal Centipede.description: A many-legged dark centipede with glassy amber mineral plates and long jointed antennae. It follows seepage and vibrations through mine cracks. Its armored back has gaps between segments; driving it toward a supported side passage can avoid fighting beneath an unstable brace.

Stone-Eating Centipede.name: Stone-Eating Centipede
Stone-Eating Centipede.description: A heavy gray segmented cave predator with grinding mouth plates and pale sensing whiskers. It rasps tracks through soft seams and can undermine loose rock. Deep occupied galleries are optional dangerous ground; an ordinary miner does not inherit its level or tier.

Storm-Kite Tengu.name: Storm-Kite Tengu
Storm-Kite Tengu.description: A gray-blue feathered adult tengu with long kite-like wings, dark eyes and a pale hooked beak. Conductive ornaments rattle along its flight feathers. It uses wind and limited electrical releases around exposed ridges; it must land, see and recover like a real opponent.

Whitefall Crane.name: Whitefall Crane
Whitefall Crane.description: A tall white mana crane with black wing tips, pale gold eyes and narrow green-blue streamers trailing from its crown feathers. It inhabits water edges and makes short startling sound calls. It is a living creature, not automatically Oroha or a tame spiritual guide.

Snow-Mantle Tengu.name: Snow-Mantle Tengu
Snow-Mantle Tengu.description: An adult white-and-charcoal feathered mountain yokai with heavy talons, a narrow beaked face and a cloak of insulating down. It claims sheltered ledges, seeks food and can negotiate passage. Cold terrain familiarity is not invulnerability to every Ice spell.

Ice-Reed Serpent.name: Ice-Reed Serpent
Ice-Reed Serpent.description: A long dark aquatic mana beast with translucent reedlike dorsal fins, silver eyes and a broad flattened jaw. Its fins scrape across thin ice before its body rises. It hunts vibration and movement in cold water rather than appearing instantly on a refuge floor.

Snowburrow Mukade.name: Snowburrow Mukade
Snowburrow Mukade.description: A broad white-plated centipede with red seam markings and two long black antennae. It travels below snow over loose ground, leaving a settling trough and a dry scraping noise. A raised moraine or prepared hard platform limits its approach.

Hollow War Armor.name: Hollow War Armor
Hollow War Armor.description: An empty lacquered armor frame tied around a residual Soul working. Its joints creak and its head follows an old guard line; it may repeat orders or resist entry. Determine whether it carries a conscious spirit rather than assuming every animated frame contains a person.

Paper-Face Moth.name: Paper-Face Moth
Paper-Face Moth.description: A thumb-to-palm-sized ivory moth with ink-like spots resembling a little face and delicate serrated wing edges. It feeds on damp paper fibers and gathers near fresh paste. Most are nuisance wildlife, with small finite groups and ordinary practical countermeasures.

Granary Rat.name: Granary Rat
Granary Rat.description: An ordinary small brown-gray rat with dark eyes and a pale belly. It steals accessible food, hides behind shelving and escapes when threatened. Beginner jobs use one exposed weak rat at a time and practical gaps, not an elite swarm or compulsory disease outbreak.

Whisper-Reed Oniwa.name: Whisper-Reed Oniwa
Whisper-Reed Oniwa.description: A reed-bodied spirit with long leaf fingers, a hollow stem throat and shifting pale eye marks. It repeats a few heard sounds to draw attention into wet ground. Touch, observation and a changed route can expose its trick; it cannot know private memories it never encountered.

Reed-Jaw Kappa.name: Reed-Jaw Kappa
Reed-Jaw Kappa.description: A squat river yokai with dark green pebbled skin, broad webbed feet, a dull shell and a flat reed-fringed head basin. Adults have varied temperaments and can bargain over a real crossing; a powerful grip and water familiarity make a hostile one dangerous. It is not automatically a childlike mascot.

Orchard Sootling.name: Orchard Sootling
Orchard Sootling.description: A little black-furred round creature with enormous pale eyebrows, tiny paws and a warm amber belly. It hides among fruit baskets and licks sweet spills. Usually mischievous, easily redirected and not a disguised high-level assassin.

Paddy Mudling.name: Paddy Mudling
Paddy Mudling.description: A small wet clay body with pebble eyes, broad paddle feet and a sprout on its head. It blocks a channel to hold a comfortable pool. Moving water, a more attractive puddle or a careful physical removal can solve a nuisance without battle.

Lantern Prowler.name: Lantern Prowler
Lantern Prowler.description: A lean long-legged predator with bark-brown fur, two pale lamps of eyes and a split tufted tail. Its flank markings break its outline among hanging lanterns. Rustles and briefly reflected eyes give warning; it is not a free unseen opening critical attack.

Root-Back Nue.name: Root-Back Nue
Root-Back Nue.description: A heavy forest beast with a primate-like face, feline forequarters, a long scaled tail and pale rootlike growths along its dark back. It waits on overhead roots and attacks from a committed pounce. Its strange body is not proof of limitless abilities or a secret human identity.

Mist-Lure Wisp.name: Mist-Lure Wisp
Mist-Lure Wisp.description: A floating knot of pale blue light around a tiny dark seed. It repeats short heard calls and drifts above unsafe ground. The voice can be tested by echoes and line of sight. It does not erase a character’s recorded memories, move inventory or teleport the party.

Marsh-Stilt Haunt.name: Marsh-Stilt Haunt
Marsh-Stilt Haunt.description: A narrow spirit body balanced on four extremely long black reed legs, with a pale hanging veil around two golden eyes. It crosses deep marsh pools and probes close movement with its front legs. Dry raised ground denies part of its reach.

Echo-Hide Stalker.name: Echo-Hide Stalker
Echo-Hide Stalker.description: A low six-legged predator with slate-blue skin, a smooth eyeless brow and pale listening membranes along its sides. It hunts repeated vibration and can mimic a short sound. It has no private knowledge of the person whose voice it resembles.

Empty Festival Husk.name: Empty Festival Husk
Empty Festival Husk.description: An animated festival effigy with a hollow reed torso, torn bright cloth and a painted wooden face. A residual working repeats a limited procession or invitation. It may accept a properly ended ritual or need physical disruption; it is not every lost ancestor at once.

Tanuki Wayfarer.name: Tanuki Wayfarer
Tanuki Wayfarer.description: An adult raccoon-dog yokai with expressive animal features, a thick tail and practical borrowed clothing. Individuals may use modest Illusion workings and enjoy bargaining or mischief. They cannot create permanent money from leaves or automatically turn into any named person.

Awakened Bell.name: Awakened Bell
Awakened Bell.description: An old bell given movement and personality through a particular history. Its metal body, cords and chime establish its anatomy rather than an added human torso. A ringing interruption and petty mischief are plausible; authority over all spirits is not.

Hush Crane.name: Hush Crane
Hush Crane.description: A rare intelligent crane spirit with actual wings, long legs and an individual attachment to a place or agreement. Identity, disposition and history belong to the actual being. Oroha is the authored crane at its crossing; do not generate replacements with its name or role.

Riftlimb Stalker.name: Riftlimb Stalker
Riftlimb Stalker.description: Reserved anatomical classification for the unique authored Hagire: a towering woman-shaped forest yokai with two long arms, two long legs, a ragged split mouth and joints that can unseat and reset. Do not spawn copies or use this as a renewable random encounter. Use Hagire’s actual record, whereabouts, hostility and resolved condition.
